name: Apex
notes: Competition platform: solvers install the uv-based `apex` CLI (install_cli.sh) and submit solution files; evaluation runs in validator-side sandboxes. text_clustering competition sandbox is explicitly 'CPU only - no GPU available'. Separate aurelius_steering competition is scored on a validator-provisioned GPU fleet (shared/competition/src/competition/aurelius_steering/README.md:67), not on miner hardware. Only 2 active miners, 52.7% burn.

name: DSperse
notes: Rust binaries (sn2-miner/sn2-validator) with docker compose as the recommended path, or prebuilt binary + PM2. README.md:24 states zk proving is CPU-intensive and 'open[s] the opportunity for non-GPU miners to participate'. Miner hardware table (README.md:239-243) lists only CPU 8-core 3.2GHz / 32GB RAM / storage, no GPU row. Highest burn in batch at 82.6%; real work is building circuitizable zk-ML models.

name: deprecated
notes: REWORKED: repo_url was the non-resolvable placeholder 'https://github.com/username/repo' -> 'unknown'; it is not a real repo, so it must not be recorded as one. clone_state re-verified by SSH on 2026-08-11: `ls -la ~/atlas/var/fleet/clones/3` returned 'No such file or directory', so clone_state stays 'missing' and is accurate. Subnet name is 'deprecated'; nothing was ever cloned and nothing is inspectable, so all repo-derived fields remain 'unknown' (setup_complexity intentionally 'unknown' rather than a low/med/high value).

name: Targon
notes: Go codebase; mining requires installing TargonOS, a signed purpose-built OS that wipes every eligible disk on dedicated bare metal (docs/miner/miner.md:57-59). Auction classes are TDX-VM-NVIDIA-H200 (line 24) and TDX-VM-NVIDIA-B200 (line 30) with min_cluster_size 8, i.e. datacenter confidential-compute GPU fleets. No VRAM figure stated in-repo. Not viable for small operators.

name: Hone
notes: ARC-AGI-2 solver competition. README.md:3: miners do not run solvers directly, they point to a git repo whose solution is executed in a validator-operated secure GPU sandbox, so no miner-side GPU is strictly needed. However README.md:99 lists 'NVIDIA GPU + drivers (for sandbox runner / local testing)' and README.md:593 sets MINER_WEIGHT_CLASS default 1xH200 for the validator-side allocation; sandbox_runner/README.md:58-59 documents an 8x H200 pool. Local iteration effectively wants a GPU. Clone is stale (last commit 2026-01-29) relative to the rest of the batch.

name: Numinous
notes: Forecasting subnet. Mining = writing an agent run by the validator sandbox; docs/miner-setup.md:45-51 lists only Python 3.11+, an editor, the numi CLI and gateway API keys as system requirements. CHANGELOG.md:252 records that torch was switched to the CPU version to shrink the env. Validator specs (docs/validator-setup.md:22-28) are CPU/RAM/disk only. Ongoing cost is LLM API keys (OpenAI/OpenRouter etc), not hardware. 0% burn, 19 miners, best prune_rank in batch (22).

name: Vanta
notes: Proprietary trading signals network. docs/miner.md:505-506 states '2 vCPU + 8 GB memory' and 'Run the miner using CPU'. Python 3.10 + requirements.txt (no torch), run.sh / pm2. Infrastructure is trivial; the difficulty is entirely the trading strategy and live market data feeds (MT5, CB Pro/Binance per docs/miner.md), plus a collateral SDK dependency.

name: TrajectoryRL
notes: Mining = authoring a SKILL.md pack, uploading it to any HTTP endpoint and committing on-chain. README.md:49 and README.md:112 both state 'No GPU, no server, no uptime required'. Miner Dockerfile is python:3.10-slim (docker/Dockerfile.miner:6). Local eval needs Docker, an LLM API key and ~10GB disk (README.md:143). Only 1 active miner, 0% burn.

name: Data Universe
notes: docs/miner.md:9: 'Miners do not require a GPU and should be able to run on a low-tier machine, as long as it has sufficient network bandwidth and disk space.' requirements.txt:11 pins torch==2.7.1 but with no CUDA/+cu marker. Complexity comes from scraping credentials and storage: Apify, Reddit (asyncpraw), YouTube API, HuggingFace uploads, S3 validation, plus dynamic desirability tuning. 70.7% burn with 239 miners means a crowded field.

name: ORO
notes: Shopping-agent benchmark. Miners submit a Python agent with agent_main(); validators execute it in a Docker sandbox built from python:3.10-slim with no CUDA (docker/sandbox/Dockerfile:1). docker/validator/pyproject.toml:24-29 pins torch to the explicit 'pytorch-cpu' index, i.e. CPU-only wheels. Validator needs 16+ GB RAM, 32 recommended (README.md:44); no GPU line anywhere and no GPU reservations in docker-compose.yml. Highest registration cost in batch (0.2558), 0% burn, 81 miners.
